title: ShelfSort — Sort Order Injection
objective: The book list can be sorted by a column of your choice. A claim code is stored in a table the page never queries — recover it and claim it.

verifier.condition: The correct claim code — present only in a hidden table and different for every instance — is submitted to the claim form.

weakness: A user-chosen sort expression is concatenated into an ORDER BY clause, where UNION cannot be used, but a conditional sort key turns the order of the results into a yes/no channel.
seededData: SQLite: books table (5 rows, prices ordered differently from titles) and a hidden vault table with a per-instance 6-character claim code. Claim attempts are limited to 10 wrong guesses.
hints: A UNION cannot follow an ORDER BY. What else can you put where a column name goes?
Look at what changes in the response when the database evaluates something different — even if the page never shows the data itself.
The first book in the list is enough to tell two sort orders apart.
burpNotes: Send a sort request to Repeater and watch which book comes first for different sort values. Errors are hidden, so a request that fails looks different from one that succeeds. Claim attempts are limited, so script the extraction rather than guessing.
